In order to realize the evils entailed by incarceration in Newgate in these days, it is necessary to give some account of its interior as it was occupied and appropriated in eighteen ten. Full details of the arrangements are to be found in Mr. Neild's "State of Prisons in England, Scotland, and Wales," published in eighteen twelve. The jail at that date was divided into eight separate and more or less distinct departments, each of which had its own wards and yard.

Two other wards were appropriated to the master's side debtors; they were each twenty-three feet by fourteen and a half, and supposed to accommodate twenty persons. The eight remaining wards were for the common side debtors, long narrow rooms -- one thirty-six feet, six twenty-three feet, and the eighth eighteen, the whole about fifteen feet wide.
